results.title: An honest look at OpusClip reviews (2025): The good, bad & ugly | eesel AI
results.content:
### The bad: You have little control, and it's glitchy

The biggest complaint you'll see is about the AI's blind spots. It just doesn't get nuance, comedic timing, or sarcasm, which are often the exact things that make a clip worth sharing. Users also talk about slow processing times and a clunky editor that makes fixing the AI's mistakes feel like a real chore.

A lot of creators get frustrated because they end up spending more time correcting the AI than it would have taken to just find and edit the clips themselves from the start. This really highlights a problem with these kinds of "black box" AI tools, if you can't tell the AI what to do or easily fix its output, you're just stuck with whatever it gives you.

### The ugly: Billing and customer support nightmares [...] Sadly, if you look at reviews on sites like Creatify.ai or in different online communities, you'll see a lot of complaints about the scheduler. Posts don't go through, accounts get disconnected, and a lot of creators just end up downloading the clips and posting them the old-fashioned way. This kind of defeats the purpose of the whole "autopilot" thing.

Here’s a quick summary table based on all that feedback. [...] ### The ugly: Billing and customer support nightmares

And this is where things get really bad. Take a quick look at OpusClip’s Trustpilot page, and you'll see a sea of one-star reviews all saying the same things. These aren't just small bugs; they're fundamental problems that make it hard to trust the company.

The most common complaints are pretty scary:

 People being charged for subscriptions after they've already canceled.
 Customer support that's basically non-existent. You get automated replies and find it almost impossible to reach an actual person.
 A cancellation process that seems designed to be as confusing and difficult as possible.

results.content:
# I'm having an issue with clips suddenly not working

Hello!  
I hope you’re all doing well! :slight_smile:  
First and foremost, I’m new to shotcut. In fact, I’m new to editing in general (aside from the basic cropping of videos and what not), so I hope you could be patient with me…

:slight_smile:

I’m having an issue that I’d love if you could help me with cuz it could potentially be devastating for work progression. [...] Currently I’m somehow working it out by:

Issues with this method:  
1- It’s scary cuz who knows what I might or might not be able to copy for whatever reason.  
2- I can’t copy markers that I had in the faulty instance to the older, working instance.  
3- It’s slow especially if you’re copying/deleting a lot of clips.  
4- It’s tedious as you might have many small segmented clips on the different timelines that you have to zoom in and out and click on each of them.

So yeah I’d highly appreciate if someone could help me understand the root of this problem to begin with, so that I can stop it from happening or at least quickly fix it in case it happened. [...] I’ve attached to this post the 2 instances “Faulty/correct instances”. The only differences are that the clip at time “00:01:07:07” is working in the correct instance, and not working in faulty instance, and that the faulty instance has more markers on it.  
Elden Ring best\_funniest moments (Correct Tree sentinel death).mlt (311.4 KB)  
Elden Ring best\_funniest moments (Faulty tree sentinel death.).mlt (318.7 KB)

UPDATE!  
I just found out, it’s only happening to clips that I have used the filter time: Remap on.  
I do it to keep the clip frozen on a specific frame for some time, as per this guide: Continue last frame of clip until next clip - #5 by MusicalBox
